races.title: State House, District 46
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Brenden H. Jones
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 46 since January 2017, and House Majority Leader since 2025. Born and raised in Columbus County, he took over his family's car dealership in the late 1990s. He has also run an auto body shop and a funeral home. He lives in Tabor City.
cands.gaps: We found no documented public statements by Jones on data centers or on development. His only issue statements in the pages we had were broad lines from an older campaign site: keeping taxes low, reining in government spending, supporting teachers, and fighting for rural transportation. They were too general to match to specific policy areas. We did not find his positions or actions on homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, immigration and H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice. We found no reported controversies or foreign ties. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We could not find a source for when his family's dealership was founded or for his education.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Columbus County and still lives in Tabor City, in his district.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has served in the NC House since 2017 and became Majority Leader in 2025. He has chaired the House Appropriations and Transportation committees. He has also owned and run a car dealership, an auto body shop and a funeral home since the late 1990s.
qual.why: He has nine years of legislative service and chamber leadership as Majority Leader, plus experience as a business owner. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score. He has no law or formal policy career in the sources.

cands.name: Brittany Newton
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 46 (Columbus and Robeson Counties). Whiteville native, U.S. Army veteran (2012–2019) and human resources professional. Single mother of two. Has not held elective office.

endorsements.text: Run for Something (listed by Ballotpedia among her endorsements and voter guide recommendations)

cands.gaps: We found no record of Newton holding public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun policy or abortion. Her birthplace, upbringing and work history rest on her own statements; no independent source confirmed them. The sources did not give details of her HR career, such as employers or years. The cut-off campaign issues page may include material we could not read.

local.label: Roots 100: In her Ballotpedia survey she says she was born and raised in Whiteville and is raising her children there, and her campaign site says she was born and raised in Columbus County; both are self-reported, and Ballotpedia lists Whiteville High School.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Eight years in the U.S. Army (2012–2019), then work as a human resources professional. She says she has organized around economic opportunity and community development in rural North Carolina. She has held no elected office and no legislative or budget role.
qual.why: She has a real work history (military service and HR), but no legislative, policy-staff or budget experience and no local elected office, so she scores in the low-to-middle range for writing law and the state budget.
